records.statement: A hypertrophy exercise catalogue should distinguish broad muscle regions by their main joint actions before mapping exercises to them.
records.applies_to: SportRX educational muscle-region and movement-pattern taxonomy for generally healthy adults.
allowed_language: SportRX groups exercises by broad anatomical region and movement task.
A muscle region may require more than one movement family for practical coverage.
disallowed_language: The catalogue target label proves that an exercise isolates a muscle.
This anatomical map diagnoses weakness, imbalance or pain.
records.limitations: Foundational anatomy supports names and actions, not hypertrophy efficacy, exercise superiority, dose or individual suitability.

records.statement: Movement families are a practical coverage layer between muscle labels and individual exercise variants, but they do not quantify stimulus to each participating muscle.
records.applies_to: SportRX exercise discovery, substitutions and hypertrophy education.
allowed_language: Horizontal push covers the pectorals with anterior-deltoid and triceps contribution.
A movement family can have several equipment-specific variants.
disallowed_language: Every set gives identical effective-set credit to every listed secondary muscle.
Movement-category coverage is a validated hypertrophy score.
records.limitations: The coverage map is an expert-curated taxonomy, not a direct physiological measurement or validated scoring system.

records.statement: Exercise variation may influence regional hypertrophy and strength when applied systematically, while excessive random or redundant variation may compromise adaptation.
records.applies_to: Healthy adults selecting or rotating resistance-training exercise variants.
allowed_language: Use anatomical and biomechanical reasoning to choose complementary exercise families.
Keep a stable variant long enough to learn and track it before changing without a clear reason.
disallowed_language: Muscle confusion is required for growth.
Changing exercises every session is superior.
One exercise is proven to maximize every region of a muscle.
records.limitations: The review included only eight studies and 241 young men; exercise-specific regional findings do not generalize to every user or muscle.

records.statement: Free weights and machines can both support hypertrophy; equipment choice should reflect goals, preference, access and the ability to perform and progress the exercise consistently.
records.applies_to: Healthy adults choosing between free-weight and machine-based resistance exercise.
allowed_language: A machine variation can be a valid alternative to a free-weight variation.
Strength records are specific to the exercise and device used.
disallowed_language: Free weights always build more muscle.
Machines always isolate a muscle better.
Loads from different machines and free-weight variants are directly comparable.
records.limitations: Only five studies in the meta-analysis reported hypertrophy, and equivalent average outcomes do not make techniques or individual tolerability identical.

records.statement: Range of motion is an exercise-selection and technique variable; full range has more favorable lower-limb hypertrophy evidence, but no single range can be prescribed universally without exercise and individual context.
records.applies_to: Healthy adults performing resistance exercise across different ranges of motion.
allowed_language: Record and repeat a controlled range of motion for the selected exercise.
Full range is a reasonable default where the movement can be performed with control and without a separate constraint.
disallowed_language: Deeper is always better for every person and exercise.
Partial range never supports hypertrophy.
SportRX can determine a pain-free range from catalogue data.
records.limitations: Upper-body evidence was limited and conflicting, and the literature does not determine an individual's safe range or account for pain.

records.statement: Training at longer average muscle lengths may modestly influence regional hypertrophy, but current evidence is small, uncertain and not sufficient for deterministic exercise rankings.
records.applies_to: Young healthy adults in resistance-training studies manipulating range of motion or exercise selection.
allowed_language: Muscle length is one factor to consider when selecting complementary exercise variants.
Regional hypertrophy evidence should be presented with uncertainty.
disallowed_language: The longest-muscle-length exercise is always best.
A specific exercise guarantees distal muscle growth.
Stretch sensation proves a superior hypertrophy stimulus.
records.limitations: Twelve studies in young adults produced small or trivial estimates with uncertainty; muscles, methods and regions differed.

records.statement: Exercise order mainly favors strength gains in exercises placed earlier; current evidence does not show a clear hypertrophy advantage for a universal multi-joint-first or single-joint-first order.
records.applies_to: Healthy adults arranging resistance exercises within a session.
allowed_language: Place the highest-priority skill or strength exercise earlier when quality matters.
Exercise order can follow the session's main priority rather than a fixed compound-first rule.
disallowed_language: Compound exercises must always come first for hypertrophy.
Pre-exhaustion is proven to produce more muscle growth.
records.limitations: The number of hypertrophy studies was limited; findings do not define an individual session order or fatigue threshold.

records.statement: Single-joint and multi-joint exercises can both support muscle and strength adaptations; isolation work is a contextual option rather than a universal requirement or universally redundant addition.
records.applies_to: Healthy adults choosing time-efficient or region-focused resistance exercise combinations.
allowed_language: Use multi-joint movements for broad coverage and add single-joint work when a goal, region or practical constraint justifies it.
A time-limited plan may rely more heavily on multi-joint movements.
disallowed_language: Isolation exercises are always necessary for growth.
Compound exercises always fully cover every contributing muscle.
Single-joint exercises are always safer.
records.limitations: Comparative evidence is small, often upper-limb focused and cannot determine the optimal exercise mix for every muscle or trainee.
